title: Signals
summary: An in-process event bus with subscribe, once and unsubscribe.

tasks.title: A handler that never fires
brief: The app registers a one-off “ready” handler and then a permanent one. On the first “ready” event the permanent handler does not run, and emit reports 1 handler called instead of 2.
Find the cause and fix it so that removing handlers while an event is being emitted never skips anyone.
done: Every handler subscribed when emit starts is called exactly once for that emit.
Handlers added during an emit wait for the next one.
emit returns the number of handlers it called.

questions: If a handler unsubscribes a later handler mid-emit, should the later one still run this time? (Snapshot semantics: yes. Confirm it with the interviewer.)
Should handlers added during an emit run in the same emit? (No.)
orient: README rules: order of subscription, once runs one time, emit returns the count.
once wraps the handler and calls off before calling it, so emit and off are the two places to read.
trace: Hypothesis: off mutates the array emit is walking. i = 0 runs the once wrapper, which splices index 0 out; the “always” handler shifts to index 0 and the loop moves on to i = 1, past it.
Confirmed by logging list.length inside the loop: 2, then the loop ends after one call.
wrapUp: Cause: emit iterated the live handler array while once/unsubscribe spliced it.
Fix: iterate a copy taken at the start of emit. That also makes handlers added mid-emit wait for the next emit.
Trade-off: one array copy per emit, which is fine for UI event volumes.

tasks.title: Wildcard listeners
brief: The analytics widget wants to hear every event. Add bus.onAny(handler), where handler receives (event, payload). It returns an unsubscribe function, like on.
Wildcard handlers run after the specific handlers for the event. emit’s return value includes them. count(event) still counts only specific handlers.
done: onAny handlers see every emit, after the specific handlers.
The unsubscribe function works; emit counts wildcard calls; count() does not.
The new type is exported from src/index.ts.

questions: Does emit’s count include wildcards? (Yes; count(event) does not.)
orient: index.ts is the public surface, so a new AnyHandler type belongs there too.
Copied the shape of on(): push, then return a closure that removes the handler.
trace: emit already snapshots its handlers; snapshot the wildcard list the same way, for the same reason.
wrapUp: Added onAny with its own list, snapshotted in emit, and exported the type.
With more time: an offAny for symmetry, and error isolation so one throwing handler does not stop the rest.
